title: Review Intent's use of .md files and /in-* skills for the v3 release
objective: Root-and-branch review of (a) the Intent-canon .md files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, restart.md, wip.md, usage-rules.md, and the rest of the default bootstrap set) and (b) the /in-* skills: what is in each, why, and what for -- then rationalise. Intent and LLMs have both come a long way since these were written; the set carries baggage, some of it stale, some of it wrong (correctable), some of it misguided (leads users and LLMs down the wrong path -- worse than wrong).
context:
hv, 2026-08-28, on the two halves: (.md files) "We're carrying a lot of baggage there. We really need to go thru the default, Intent-canon .md files and do a root-and-branch review of what's in them, why, and what for. I suspect we have a _lot_ of rationalisation that can be done." (/in-* skills) "Many of these make no sense any more and some of the others are not just out of date, but potentially wrong, or worse, misguided (wrong can be corrected, misguided will lead users and the LLMs down the wrong path)."

Primary source material is vendored in this thread at `_sources/`: the transcript and companion of 'Mastering Claude Code in 30 minutes' (Boris Cherny, Anthropic, creator of Claude Code) -- to be read as the current-state reference for how Claude Code actually consumes CLAUDE.md, skills, and project context, against which the canon set is judged. Sequencing: primed 2026-08-28, work starts after the Conflab hoist tail closes (hv). Related threads primed the same day: ST0066 (fiat close), ST0067 (intent llm). The skills half should also settle the known mechanical debts where they surface: the skill-sync SKILL.md-only checksum blind spot, and the renderer's $N-stripping trap.
